rules.title: New Jersey Security Deposit Law
rules.requirement: Landlords may collect a security deposit of at most 1.5 times one month's rent, with yearly increases capped at 10% of the current deposit. Deposits are held in trust in interest-bearing accounts, interest belongs to the tenant, and the landlord must give written notice of the bank, amount and rate.
rules.key_value: 1.5 months' rent maximum; annual increase at most 10% of current deposit
rules.penalty: If the tenant does not get proper notice or interest, the tenant may apply the deposit plus 7% per annum interest to rent.
rules.status_basis: Described as existing law in the NJ DCA publication.

coverage.summary: Applies to most residential rental properties, including mobile homes.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are exempt unless the tenant requests application 30 days after written request.

rules.quoted_span:
The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than 
one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ). It can be less.
